# Behavioral Specification: TL-UL Error Responder

## 1. Purpose

The module is a TileLink-UL device endpoint that responds to every accepted request with an error response. It is intended for situations where a request cannot be forwarded to a valid destination and must be terminated with a bus error.

The module performs no address decoding, no data storage, and no register access. It simply accepts requests and returns an error.

## 2. General Behavior

- The module shall be idle after reset.
- While idle, it shall be ready to accept a request.
- A request is accepted when the request valid and request ready signals are both asserted at a clock edge.
- For every accepted request, the module shall generate exactly one response.
- The response shall be asserted as an error response.
- The module shall not generate a response unless a request has been accepted.

## 3. Request Acceptance

Request acceptance shall be controlled by the standard TileLink-UL valid/ready handshake.

The module shall accept a request whenever it is able to do so. The only condition that shall prevent acceptance of a new request is when a previously generated response is still valid and has not yet been accepted by the host.

In particular:

- If no response is currently being held, the module shall accept a request.
- If a response is being presented and the host accepts it in the same cycle, the module may also accept a new request in that same cycle.
- If a response is being presented and the host does not accept it, the module shall not accept a new request.
- Once a held response is accepted, request acceptance shall resume.

The module shall support back-to-back transactions: when each response is accepted as soon as it is presented, a new request may be accepted in every cycle.

## 4. Response Generation

For each accepted request, the module shall produce an error response with the following behavior:

- The response error indication shall be asserted.
- The response opcode shall be:
  - Read response with data for a read request.
  - Write acknowledgement for all non-read request opcodes, including undefined opcode encodings.
- The response source identifier shall match the source identifier of the accepted request.
- The response size shall match the size of the accepted request.
- The response data shall be all 1s on every response.
- The response sink, parameter, and user fields shall be zero.

The request address, request data, request mask, and request user fields shall not affect the response. The module shall ignore these fields.

## 5. Timing and Backpressure

The response for an accepted request shall be presented in the clock cycle immediately following the cycle in which the request was accepted.

If the host accepts the response in that same cycle, the transaction is complete and the module may continue accepting new requests.

If the host does not accept the response, the module shall hold the response valid until the host accepts it. While the response is being held, the module shall not accept any new requests.

After a held response is accepted, the module shall return to the idle state and resume accepting requests.

## 6. Reset Behavior

When reset is asserted, the module shall clear any pending transaction state and shall not present a response.

After reset deassertion, the module shall be idle and ready to accept a new request.

If reset asserts while a response is pending, the pending response shall be discarded. No response shall be delivered for that discarded transaction.
